newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares flat in lower trade, seen drifting.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares flat in lower trade, seen drifting.

text.p: The Polish bourse stayed flat in lighter trade and analysts said a lack of strong fundamental signals might keep the market moving sideways next week.

They said that even though a fall was possible on Friday in a reaction to a two-session significant rise, relative equilibrum reached after six weeks of falls would prevent prices from either significant falls or strong gains.

"The prices on the bourse seem adequate to the fundamental value of firms...I believe the market might stay in horizontal trend as so far there are no signals to push it either way," said Roman Sosnowski of Bank Staropolski brokerage.

Analysts said a lack of immediate reaction to Wednesday's Wall Street gains might signal Polish investors' obsession with Dow was ending but said it would take more time to judge whether Warsaw had given up tracking the U.S. market's daily movements.
The main market's WIG index was flat at 16,282.1, and turnover fell 17 percent to 144.5 million zlotys on all three markets as 39 issues fell, 22 rose and 32 were flat.
Analysts said March earnings reports, due later on Thursday and on Friday, were not expected to move the whole market in either direction but could affect individual stocks.
Some analysts said, however, a strong short-term uptrend might start as early as next week with some prospective low-caps, now trading at 15-20 times historical earnings, leading the rises.
Traders said construction company Espebepe extended the last two-session's 20-percent rise, jumping 9.3 percent as investors speculated it might succeed in clinching a debt deal with its creditors.
In the continuous trade stocks were mixed and the WIG 20 index closed at 1,608.1 points, 0.4 percent lower than at the regular session. -- Malgorzata Rzepka +48 22 653 9700
